title: Tunbridge Wells Borough Council: The Amelia Scott, Collecting Tomorrow
summary: The Amelia Scott reports 50% faster image processing, improved scans, interactive exhibits, and volunteers progressing to paid museum roles.
account: The Amelia Scott uses Adobe Lightroom AI to prepare artifact images for digital twins and tactile display objects. The council reports 50% faster scan/image processing, better scan quality, interactive exhibitions, and volunteers progressing to paid museum roles. Commercial revenue remains prospective, and visitor learning gains are unmeasured. Training, partnerships, and digital production contribute jointly to the results. AI’s effect on employment and learning is unknown.
purpose: Improve artifact-imaging workflows and create digital and tactile museum experiences.
system: Adobe Lightroom generative-AI functions within The Amelia Scott’s 3D scanning and digital-twin workflow
deployer: Tunbridge Wells Borough Council, The Amelia Scott

ratings.reason: Improved digital twins and delivered interactive and tactile exhibits extend the museum’s capabilities.
The source reports skill development, volunteers obtaining paid roles, and expanded ways to experience artifacts. These are capability/opportunity gains without established livelihood preservation.

ai_role.statement: The source attributes faster masking, editing, and improved scan preparation to Lightroom AI within a broader production workflow. Training, partnerships, and other tools also contribute, so employment and visitor-learning effects cannot be isolated to AI.

evidence.citation: Council or project account published in the Local Government Association AI case-study bank. The account provides no independent outcome evaluation.
